_comment: THE PROBE CATALOGUE. This file is data, not code — it is the list of real places
the engine goes and looks, and the rule for reading what came back.
Every signature below was verified against live endpoints on 2026-08-05. If a
platform changes its 404 page, you fix THIS file, not the engine.
A place resolves to one of three outcomes:
hit          — the thing exists here (status ok AND a positive marker matched)
miss         — the thing is not here (definitive 404/410, or a negative marker)
inconclusive — we learned nothing (403, 429, 5xx, timeout, robots-blocked,
or 200 with no marker either way)
kind:
first_party  — the creator's own surface. At least one of these must be READ
before ANY item may resolve to verified_absent (see resolve.js).
guess        — a place this kind of thing usually lives.
api          — an official, documented, keyless API.
harvested    — a URL found in the creator's own bio/links (added at runtime).
neverConclusive: true means this place can be read for links but can never
decide presence or absence. Instagram is the example — a nonexistent handle
returns 200 with no distinguishing marker, so it is honestly unreadable.
Q5, 2026-08-06: store and newsletter each gained one more place — the creator's
OWN SITE. It is kind first_party because it is the most first-party surface
there is, and its domain is harvested from what they publish rather than
guessed (see lib/site.js). Its markers were chosen against live pages on
2026-08-06 and each one is listed with the trap it had to survive.
Q5 — how the creator's own domain is found, and how much of it is read.
Discovery has one test and two sources: the domain has to CARRY THEIR NAME,
and they have to have published it — as a link, or as the address in their
bio. notTheirOwn removes the platforms they merely have an account on before
either source is read. minNameOverlap is the length below which a name match
is a coincidence.
The name test is not decoration. Without it, Veritasium's TikTok bio link
(ankerfast.club, an Anker campaign URL) read as his own site on 6 Aug 2026 and
put Anker's Shopify cart on his report as his store. The link-in-bio slot is
where sponsors live.
maxPages caps the read at the homepage plus four pages they link to from it,
on their own domain only. When the cap bites, the place resolves inconclusive
rather than absent: a search that stopped early must not read as one that
finished.
minTextChars/minAnchors detect a page that arrives empty and fills itself in
the browser. §11.3 rules out a headless browser, so such a page is UNREAD, not
empty — the two produce opposite verdicts and the engine must not confuse them.

identity.label: TikTok profile
identity.note: TRAP, verified 2026-08-05: the string "Couldn't find this account" ships in TikTok's localisation bundle on EVERY profile page, real or not. Using it as a negative marker marks real accounts absent. The reliable discriminator is a followerCount in the rehydration blob. Signatures have to be tested in BOTH directions; this one was not, and it silently produced the exact failure PRD 5.3 is written to prevent.

identity.label: YouTube channel
identity.note: A YouTube channel page is ~2.6MB and the data we want sits past the 600KB default read cap, so this place raises it. YouTube 404s cleanly for a handle that does not exist, so status alone settles presence.

identity.label: Instagram profile
identity.note: Instagram returns 200 for handles that do not exist and exposes no reliable marker. Read for links only; never used to decide presence or absence. PRD 11.3 calls Instagram effectively closed and this is why.

identity.label: Bluesky profile
identity.note: THE ONLY PLACE IN THIS FILE WHERE A 4xx MEANS ABSENT, AND IT IS KEYED ON THE MESSAGE RATHER THAN THE STATUS. Verified in both directions 2026-08-12: a live handle returns 200 with a DID, and a handle belonging to nobody returns 400 {"error":"InvalidRequest","message":"Profile not found"}. The trap is that the SAME 400 comes back for a malformed actor — and a bare handle is malformed, because the AppView wants a DID or a full handle. Putting 400 in absent.status would therefore mark every creator absent the moment a guess was formatted wrong. So absence is the message, and any other 400 falls through to inconclusive, which is what asking the question wrong actually is. See lib/bluesky.js. NOTE ALSO that this entry only ever asks {handle}.bsky.social; a creator whose Bluesky handle is their own domain is found by lib/bluesky.js in sweep, whose answer overrides this one the same way the YouTube Data API overrides the channel page.

inventory.label: Newsletter
inventory._requiredPlacesWithOwnSite: Q5: the bar rises when their own site is one of the places, because 'we looked in 6 places including their own site' is a stronger claim than five platform guesses. It also means a creator whose site we could not read cannot reach verified_absent — we knew where to look and did not manage it, which is a not_found and says so.

places.label: substack.com/@handle
places.note: TRAP: a handle that does not exist returns 200 and redirects to a search page. finalUrlNot is what stops the engine reporting a search page as a newsletter.

places.label: their own site
places.missWhy: no way to subscribe to anything on their own site
places.note: Markers are lowercase and matched against the lowercased page source. Verified live 2026-08-06: nasa.gov and veritasium.com carry 'newsletter' and both have one; mkbhd.com and smosh.com carry a Klaviyo signup. THE TRAP is bare 'subscribe' — it is on veritasium.com and smosh.com and both times it means the YouTube button. Tested in both directions in test.js, which is what the TikTok signature was not.

inventory.label: Store
inventory._requiredPlacesWithOwnSite: Q5: see the newsletter note. Three platform guesses were what said MKBHD has no store while he was selling at mkbhd.com.

places.label: handle.myshopify.com
places.note: Shopify returns 403 for unclaimed subdomains, which here is a real negative rather than a block. Narrow exception, deliberate.

places.label: ko-fi.com/handle
places.note: Verified 2026-08-05: sits behind a bot wall and answers 403 to an identified client. Kept because it can still produce a hit, excluded from the absence arithmetic because a door that never opens is not a place we looked.

places.label: etsy.com/shop/handle
places.note: Verified 2026-08-05: sits behind a bot wall and answers 403 to an identified client. Kept because it can still produce a hit, excluded from the absence arithmetic because a door that never opens is not a place we looked.

places.label: their own site
places.missWhy: nothing to buy on their own site
places.note: Markers are lowercase and matched against the lowercased page source. Verified live 2026-08-06: mkbhd.com and smosh.com hit; nasa.gov and chipotle.com do not. THE TRAPS are the bare words — chipotle.com contains 'store' twice and both are 'app-store-image' and a cookie script, and veritasium.com contains 'addtocart', 'shop', 'store' and 'merch' while carrying no store at all (a Squarespace commerce config with isLive:false). So the needle is 'add to cart' with its spaces, never the concatenation. Tested in both directions in test.js.

places.label: Apple Podcasts directory
places.note: Official, documented, keyless JSON API. Presence requires a NAME match, not merely resultCount > 0 — a search for a common word returns unrelated shows.

places.label: handle.com
places.note: status 0 means DNS failure — for a domain guess that is a genuine negative, not a block.

inventory.label: Representation / management

places.label: their own bio
places.note: Deliberately weak. Public data can show that representation IS declared; it cannot show that none exists. This check resolves present or not_found, never verified_absent — which is why PRD 8 lists 'already with an agency' as the decline reason the Missing check cannot catch.

inventory.presenceOnlyWhy: Can show this IS there, never that it is not — the evidence is a sample or a self-declaration. Excluded from the confidence denominator (Q1); named on the report instead.

inventory.presenceOnlyWhy: Can show this IS there, never that it is not — the evidence is a sample or a self-declaration. Excluded from the confidence denominator (Q1); named on the report instead.

inventory.presenceOnlyWhy: Can show this IS there, never that it is not — the evidence is a sample or a self-declaration. Excluded from the confidence denominator (Q1); named on the report instead.

inventory.label: Platform subscriptions
inventory.requiresApi: Platform subscription status is only visible through partner APIs we do not have. Resolves not_found and says so.

inventory.label: Shopping tags
inventory.requiresApi: Shopping-tag status is only visible through partner APIs we do not have. Resolves not_found and says so.
